title: Applied ML Evals: End-to-End Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Malik
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines Redwood's standard end-to-end process for model onboarding and continuous evaluation: how models are validated in the eval harness, how prompt sets and benchmarks are curated, how quantization profiles are generated and validated, and how regression triage is performed when quality drops are detected. This document is the canonical cross-functional reference for ML engineers, applied ML, and SREs involved in production model rollout.

Scope: covers hosted and dedicated model variants used in Redwood API (text generation and chat), integration with the eval harness, prompt set lifecycle, quantization generation & validation, and the regression triage runbook. Does not replace per-customer private-deployment compliance steps or security baggage handling.

Table of contents
1. Ownership and roles
2. Eval harness pipeline (CI and nightly)
3. Prompt sets and benchmark standards
4. Model onboarding acceptance criteria
5. Quantization profile generation & validation
6. Regression detection and triage runbook
7. Monitoring, dashboards, and alerts
8. Example commands and JSON snippets
9. Appendix: thresholds and templates

1) Ownership and roles
- Product: defines acceptance criteria for user-facing features and major PRDs.
- Applied ML team: owns eval harness, prompt sets, metric definitions, and regression triage coordination.
- Serving/runtime team: owns model packaging, kernel compatibility, and latency/cost validation.
- SRE/observability: dashboards, alerts, and on-call escalation.
- Release owner (rotation): responsible for final signoff on rollouts for a given model version.

2) Eval harness pipeline
Intro: The eval harness runs deterministic, reproducible evaluations against a model artifact. There are two main execution paths: CI (pre-merge) and nightly/regression pipelines (post-deploy and continuous monitoring).

CI pipeline (pre-merge):
- Trigger: PR or model artifact upload.
- Steps: unit tests -> small-sample bench (100 examples) -> safety filter check -> quick metric report.
- Gate: no critical safety failures and delta against baseline quality metrics <= 2.0% absolute drop for primary metrics.

Nightly pipeline (full evaluation):
- Trigger: nightly cron or post-deploy webhook.
- Steps: run full prompt-set catalog (see section 3), compute metrics, generate per-prompt failure traces, run quantization regression checks, and publish to the eval dashboard.
- Artifacts: per-run JSON, CSV of failures, evaluation HTML report. Location: s3://redwood-evals/{model}/{version}/{date}/.

3) Prompt sets and benchmark standards
Principles:
- Representative: prompt sets must reflect real customer workloads (sourced from anonymized request traces + curated enterprise prompts).
- Diverse: include edge cases, short/long contexts, system messages, tool-calling scenarios.
- Small smoke sets for CI (100–500 prompts), medium sets for candidate validation (1k–5k), and full sets for nightly/regression (5k–50k).

Prompt set metadata (required fields for each set):
- name (string)
- intended_task (generation|chat|embedding|summarization|rerank)
- size_category (smoke|medium|full)
- source (anonymized-traces|curated|third-party-benchmark)
- owner (team-email)

Curation process (high level):
1. Create prompt set with clear intent and labeling schema.
2. Review by applied-ml (responsible) and product (optional) for coverage.
3. Add to catalog with tags and owners.
4. Run against baseline model to establish golden metrics.

Quality labels used in benchmark annotations: correct, partially_correct, irrelevant, harmful, hallucinated, format_error.

4) Model onboarding acceptance criteria
Minimum gates before a model variant is eligible for rollout to any production tier:
- Functional: passes CI harness with smoke set, safety checks, and unit tests.
- Quality: for primary workload, no metric regression > 1.0% absolute for accuracy-style metrics OR relative BLEU/ROUGE drops <= 2.0% where applicable.
- Latency: p50 and p99 within expected range for the target tier (p99 <= 3x baseline p99).
- Cost: estimated per-token cost within configured budget for target tier.
- Quantization: if quantized, additional accuracy checks (see section 5).
- Observability: traces and debug hooks instrumented; eval artifacts stored in canonical S3 path.
- Signoff: release owner + applied-ml reviewer approval.

Onboarding checklist (actionable):
- [ ] Register model artifact in model registry (artifact id).
- [ ] Run CI eval harness and attach report.
- [ ] Produce quantization profile if applicable.
- [ ] Complete runbook for rollback and fallback model.
- [ ] Create dashboard tile with baseline comparisons.
- [ ] Schedule canary rollout plan (percentages and duration).

5) Quantization profile generation & validation
Overview: quantization profiles are generated using representative calibration sets and validated against evaluation prompt sets. Profiles include per-layer calibration stats, chosen bitwidth (int8, int4, q4_K_M, etc.), and tuning knobs.

Generation steps:
1. Choose calibration set (prefer medium/full prompt set with diverse token distributions).
2. Run calibration tooling: collect activation distributions, per-channel histograms, and outlier stats.
3. Generate candidate profiles for target bitwidths (e.g., q8, q4, q4_k_m).
4. Run the quantized model through CI and nightly eval harness.

Validation criteria:
- Functional correctness: no crashes or runtime exceptions on standard workloads.
- Quality threshold: primary metric regression <= 1.0% absolute vs FP16 baseline OR task-specific delta <= tolerance specified by product.
- Regression triage check: run automated diff to detect categories of failure (format, hallucination, truncation).
- Latency/cost: quantized variant must meet cost/latency expectations for the target tier.

If a candidate profile fails, either: tune per-layer scales, try hybrid quantization (partially quantize FP16 sensitive layers), or revert to higher-precision profile. Document candidate decisions in the quantization profile YAML and attach to model registry.

6) Regression detection and triage runbook
Alerting rules (examples):
- Quality alert: nightly eval shows a delta > 1.5% absolute on primary metric OR increase in harmful label rate > 40% relative.
- Canary alert: degradation observed in canary traffic with statistically significant delta (p < 0.01) on NPS or user-reported quality signals.

Initial triage (15 min):
1. Confirm alert and severity.
2. Identify model artifact and variant.
3. Pull recent eval reports from s3 and compare to previous-good baseline.
4. Run targeted smoke tests: fast-run small prompt sets that exercise observed failure modes.

Investigation steps (30–120 min):
- Check telemetry: tokenization differences, recent tokenizer updates, or preprocessing changes.
- Check quantization differences: was a new profile deployed? If yes, run FP16 vs quantized diff on suspicious prompts.
- Reproduce locally using the eval harness to capture full model traces (KV cache, logits, topk).
- Check rollout & routing: confirm that fallback rules did not route to an incompatible variant.

Escalation and mitigation:
- If root cause is model quality (e.g., regression introduced by new weights), rollback to previous model version and open a regression issue.
- If root cause is quantization, immediately revert to higher-precision variant for affected capacity or enable hybrid profile.
- If root cause is routing/config, update routing policy and re-run canary.
- For critical customer impact, notify customer-success and go-to-market leads (per escalation playbook) and create incident in PagerDuty with severity.

Postmortem and prevention:
- For any regression that caused customer-visible impact, perform a postmortem within 3 business days.
- Add failing prompts to a dedicated regression prompt set and add unit tests to CI.

7) Monitoring, dashboards, and alerts
Minimum dashboard tiles for each model variant:
- Eval quality trend (primary metric over time).
- Prompt-set failure rate by category (hallucination, format, harmful).
- Canary vs baseline comparison with statistical test results.
- Quantized vs FP16 diff summary.
- Cost and latency per token.

SLOs and thresholds (examples):
- Nightly quality regressions: auto-alert if primary metric delta > 1.5% absolute.
- Canary windows: if metric delta is statistically significant (p < 0.01) over 12 hours and effect size > 0.7%, pause rollout.

8) Example commands and JSON snippets
Register an artifact (CLI):
- redwood model register --artifact ./model-v2.tar.gz --name "gpt-lite-v2" --tags "quantized,q4_k_m"
Run CI eval harness locally (Docker):
- docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/work redwood/eval-harness:latest --model /work/model-v2 --prompt-set prompts/summarization-smoke.json --out report.json
Sample eval report (JSON summary):
- {
  "model": "gpt-lite-v2",
  "version": "2026-11-10",
  "primary_metric": "ROUGE-L",
  "primary_metric_value": "0.412",
  "baseline_value": "0.419",
  "delta": "-0.007 ( -1.67% )"
}

9) Appendix: thresholds and templates
- Primary metric regression tolerance: 1.0% absolute for classification-like accuracy; 2.0% relative for BLEU/ROUGE-style metrics unless product specifies otherwise.
- Safety/harmful threshold: any increase in harmful label rate > 10% absolute triggers an immediate high-priority investigation.
- Canary rollout template: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 24–48 hour windows and automatic pause on alerts.
